## Reasoning
Alice is unmarried and not a surviving spouse or head of household. She files as an individual under §1(a)(3)(c).

Alice's gross income is $311,510. She takes the standard deduction of $6,300 for unmarried individuals under §63(c)(2)(C), resulting in taxable income of $305,210.

Bob has no income, but there are no facts indicating Alice provides more than half of Bob's support or maintains a household for him. Therefore, Alice does not qualify as head of household and cannot claim Bob as a dependent.

Alice's taxable income of $305,210 exceeds $250,000, so under §1(a)(3)(v), the tax is $79,772 plus 39.6% of the excess over $250,000.

Tax = $79,772 + 0.396 × ($305,210 - $250,000)
Tax = $79,772 + 0.396 × $55,210
Tax = $79,772 + $21,863.16
Tax = $101,635.16, rounded to $101,635
